claims.claim: The Pont du Gard has three tiers of arches
claims.quote: The bridge has three tiers of arches made from Shelly limestone and stands 48.8 m (160 ft) high.

claims.claim: The bridge was stacked without mortar
claims.quote: The Pont du Gard was constructed largely without the use of mortar or clamps.

claims.claim: It contains 50,400 tons of limestone
claims.quote: It contains an estimated 50,400 tons of limestone with a volume of some 21,000 m3 (740,000 cu ft)

claims.claim: Blocks were cut to fit by friction and gravity alone
claims.quote: The blocks were precisely cut to fit perfectly together by friction and gravity, eliminating the need for mortar.

claims.claim: Some individual blocks weigh up to 6 tons
claims.quote: some of the individual blocks weigh up to 6 tons

claims.claim: The image arches.jpg is a postcard of Nîmes, c.1900–1910
claims.quote: Date: between 1900 and 1910

claims.claim: The postcard bears the printed caption 'NIMES — Le Pont du Gard A.R.'
claims.quote: NIMES – Le Pont du Gard  A.R.

claims.claim: The Pont du Gard descends 2.5 cm in 456 m
claims.quote: The Pont du Gard itself descends 2.5 cm (0.98 in) in 456 m (1,496 ft), a gradient of 1 in 18,241.

claims.claim: The bridge carried 40,000 cubic metres of water a day
claims.quote: The aqueduct formerly carried an estimated 40,000 m3 (8,800,000 imp gal; 11,000,000 US gal) of water a day

claims.claim: The water travelled 50 km to Nîmes
claims.quote: to carry water over 50 km (31 mi) to the Roman colony of Nemausus (Nîmes)

claims.claim: The journey took nearly 27 hours
claims.quote: It is estimated that the aqueduct supplied the city with around 40,000 cubic metres (8,800,000 imp gal) of water a day that took nearly 27 hours to flow from the source to the city.

claims.claim: Blocks were numbered and inscribed with required locations such as fronte dextra and fronte sinistra (front right, front left)
claims.quote: Many blocks were numbered and inscribed with the required locations, such as fronte dextra or fronte sinistra (front right or front left), to guide the builders.

claims.claim: Construction employed between 800 and 1,000 workers and took about fifteen years
claims.quote: It is believed to have taken about fifteen years to build, employing between 800 and 1,000 workers.

claims.claim: The upper levels of the bridge bend upstream, and this was not by deliberate design
claims.quote: It was long believed that the engineers had designed it this way deliberately to strengthen the bridge's structure against the flow of water, like a dam wall. However, a microtopographic survey carried out in 1989 showed that the bend is caused by the stone expanding and contracting by about 5 mm (0.20 in) a day under the heat of the sun.

claims.claim: A microtopographic survey in 1989 identified the cause of the bend
claims.quote: a microtopographic survey carried out in 1989 showed that the bend is caused by the stone expanding and contracting by about 5 mm (0.20 in) a day under the heat of the sun

claims.claim: In the 1620s Henri, Duke of Rohan had one side of the second row of arches cut away to about one-third of their thickness to move artillery, severely weakening the bridge
claims.quote: To make space for his artillery to cross the bridge, the duke had one side of the second row of arches cut away to a depth of about one-third of their original thickness. This left a gap on the lowest deck wide enough to accommodate carts and cannons, but severely weakened the bridge in the process.

claims.claim: The Pont du Gard survived because it served as a toll bridge
claims.quote: Its survival was due to its use as a toll bridge across the valley.

claims.claim: From the 13th century the seigneurs of Uzès, later the Bishops of Uzès, levied tolls and were responsible for keeping the bridge repaired
claims.quote: In the 13th century the French king granted the seigneurs of Uzès the right to levy tolls on those using the bridge. The right later passed to the Bishops of Uzès. In return, they were responsible for maintaining the bridge in good repair.

claims.claim: Construction has long been credited to Agrippa around 19 BC
claims.quote: The construction of the aqueduct has long been credited to the Roman emperor Augustus's son-in-law and aide, Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, around the year 19 BC.

claims.claim: Coins discovered in the Nîmes outflow are no older than the reign of Claudius
claims.quote: coins discovered in the outflow in Nîmes are no older than the reign of the emperor Claudius (41–54 AD)

claims.claim: Newer excavations point to construction between 40 and 60 AD
claims.quote: Newer excavations suggest the construction may have taken place between 40 and 60 AD.

claims.claim: The bridge is 49 m high and 274 m long
claims.quote: Built on three levels, the Pont is 49 m (161 ft) high above the river at low water and 274 m (899 ft) long.

claims.claim: Between the Pont du Gard and St Bonnet the engineers had to allow a fall of 7 mm per 100 m
claims.quote: the winding route between the Pont du Gard and St Bonnet required an extraordinary degree of accuracy from the Roman engineers, who had to allow for a fall of only 7 millimetres (0.28 in) per 100 metres (330 ft) of the conduit

claims.claim: The 1620s damage by the Duke of Rohan was the worst damage the bridge suffered
claims.quote: Although some of its stones were plundered for use elsewhere, the Pont du Gard remained largely intact. ... However, it suffered serious damage during the 1620s when Henri, Duke of Rohan made use of the bridge to transport his artillery
